High-frequency linear (7–15 MHz) grayscale and color Doppler sonography of the anterior abdominal wall was performed over the region of clinical concern at rest and during Valsalva maneuvers in supine and standing positions.
Location: Linea semilunaris at the lateral margin of the rectus abdominis.

Fascial Layer & Defect: High-frequency evaluation along the linea semilunaris demonstrates an intact Spigelian aponeurosis between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis layers. No focal fascial defect or abnormal protrusion of preperitoneal fat or bowel is identified at rest or during Valsalva maneuvers in supine and upright positions.
Hernia Sac & Contents: No hernia sac is present.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Normal adjacent musculature without diastasis. Overlying subcutaneous fat is unremarkable with no focal lipoma, fluid collection, or hyperemia.
Normal targeted abdominal wall ultrasound; no sonographic evidence of a spigelian hernia.

subs.title: Spigelian Hernia (Lateral Border of Rectus Abdominis)
items: Along the [right / left] linea semilunaris at the lateral margin of the rectus abdominis muscle, there is a defect in the Spigelian aponeurosis measuring [X.X] cm in width, allowing an interparietal hernia sac measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm containing [omental fat / bowel] to protrude between the internal oblique and external oblique layers during Valsalva (reducible at rest).

subs.title: Incarcerated vs. Strangulated Abdominal Wall Hernia
items: Incarcerated (Viable): The hernia contents are fixed and non-reducible upon graded transducer compression; however, the herniated [fat / bowel] maintains normal echogenicity, normal wall thickness, and preserved color Doppler vascularity without fluid in the hernia sac.

Strangulated (Emergency): The non-reducible hernia sac contains a thick-walled, aperistaltic, fluid-filled bowel loop (wall thickness [X.X] mm) with surrounding free fluid within the sac and absent intramural color Doppler flow, concerning for strangulation.

bank.title: PART 2: EXAMPLE FINDINGS FROM THE SAMPLE ABNORMAL REPORT
items: Left Semilunar Line (Spigelian Region): Along the lateral border of the left rectus abdominis muscle (linea semilunaris) below the level of the umbilicus, there is a second fascial defect in the transversus abdominis and internal oblique aponeurosis measuring 1.3 cm, through which a reducible left Spigelian hernia sac (2.9 x 1.7 cm) containing omental fat protrudes intraparietally beneath an intact external oblique aponeurosis during Valsalva.
Reducible left Spigelian hernia (neck width 1.3 cm, sac 2.9 cm) containing omental fat.
